title: Blind 75 — Curated LeetCode Interview Questions
tagline: The original 75-problem starter set from the Blind forum — still the most efficient way to pass a FAANG coding round.
description: Blind 75 is a hand-picked list of 75 LeetCode problems that cover every pattern interviewers rely on for a FAANG-level coding round. It originated on the Blind forum (2020) as the shortest possible path to feeling interview-ready, and it remains the single highest-leverage problem set in the industry. Work through it once, and you will have seen a canonical example of almost every pattern the interviewer is checking for. On InterviewExplainer, every problem on this list links to a line-by-line walkthrough in Java and Python — not just a submission, but the interview-voice explanation of why the approach works.
credit: Originally curated by a Meta engineer on the Blind forum.
howToUse: Do groups in order — they build on each other.
For each problem: time-box 20 minutes to attempt, then read the walkthrough.
Re-solve the same problem one week later before moving on — spaced repetition is the moat.
Switch the code panel between Java and Python depending on the language you will interview in.
After each group, say the interview-voice answer out loud without looking.
Treat any problem you solved only by reading the editorial as 'not learned yet' — re-attempt from scratch.
whyThisSheet: 75 problems is the minimum number that still exposes every major interview pattern.
Every problem on Blind 75 has been asked at a FAANG in the last 2 years.
The ordering here mirrors how interviewers build up difficulty across rounds.
Beats random LeetCode grinding by ~3x in interview-readiness per hour invested.
